article_title: Evaluating fluid and crystallized abilities in the performance of an educational process
citation: Angel Blanch. (2015). Evaluating fluid and crystallized abilities in the performance of an educational process. Springer Verlag. http://hdl.handle.net/10459.1/48328
title: Xenograde Systems instructional project (BURN11 dataset): a four-unit, one-week hierarchical learning sequence on an imaginary science
description: The instructional intervention comprised "a two-phase description of an imaginary science designated as Xenograde Systems: a lecture/discussion phase, and an individual working phase." Curricular materials spanned four hierarchical learning units delivered in booklets of four to five pages with written prose, diagrams, graphs, and tables: Unit 1 defined basic terms and operations, Unit 2 covered rules and procedures for reading graphs, Unit 3 introduced facts and concepts increasing system complexity, and Unit 4 presented the fully operating system. One multiple-choice achievement test per unit (18, 14, 16, and 16 items; reliabilities .83, .76, .80, .76) assessed knowledge, comprehension, and application.
requirements: Systematic and periodical performance assessment across the instructional sequence, as required for latent growth modeling
constraints: The article notes individual growth curves could not be modelled because raw data were not available within the BURN11 dataset, which consists of a correlation matrix
target_learners: 101 California high-school students in grades 10–12 (51 males, 50 females)
target_learning_goals: Learning novel concepts and procedures of an imaginary science system at knowledge, comprehension, and application levels
examples: The original Burns (1980) intervention found Gc related with learning throughout the intervention, whereas Gf was related with learning depending on the point in time it was measured
key_sources: Angel Blanch. (2015). Evaluating fluid and crystallized abilities in the performance of an educational process. Springer Verlag. http://hdl.handle.net/10459.1/48328

article_title: Interactive Whiteboard for Primary Schools in Mauritius: An Effective Tool or Just Another Trend?
citation: Bahadur, G. K. & Oogarah, D. (2013). Interactive whiteboard for primary schools in Mauritius: An effective tool or just another trend? IJEDICT, 9(1), 19-35. http://ijedict.dec.uwi.edu//viewarticle.php?id=1559
title: XERTE-built Solar System Educational Resource with interactive multimedia activities
description: An Educational Resource on the Solar System was built with XERTE, an open-source authoring tool from the University of Nottingham described as "a flexible template for creating interactive learning objects". It incorporated videos, MP3 sound effects for pictures, click-to-reveal and drag-and-drop activities, and formative exercises (matching, quiz, true/false, MCQ, closed test, classifying) with immediate feedback, guided by Kemp's Instructional Design Model and Gagne's Nine Events of Instruction.
requirements: A teacher able to operate the IWB and navigate the resource; the resource was used in 50-minute sessions over three days
constraints: The study used it with Standard 5 pupils (9-10 years old) in two Mauritian primary schools
target_learners: Standard 5 primary school pupils aged 9-10 in Mauritius
target_learning_goals: Understanding the Solar System (Earth, Moon and planetary orbits), part of the Standard V Science syllabus
examples: Pupils dragged words into boxes that would not accept a wrong answer, and clicked objects on the board to reveal more information
key_sources: Bahadur, G. K. & Oogarah, D. (2013). Interactive whiteboard for primary schools in Mauritius: An effective tool or just another trend? IJEDICT, 9(1), 19-35. http://ijedict.dec.uwi.edu//viewarticle.php?id=1559
